dma.scope: Safe F030/A030/L083 staged TX, finite-chunk RX and combined split TX/RX DMA with ordinary caller slices.
limitations: F030/A030/L083 with qualified SRAM metadata and clean startup admission; static UART/channel/staging owners are consumed.
CPU copy per byte and possible chunk gaps; write completes memory-to-TDR transfer and flush separately waits for the wire.
Cancellation retains each direction's current chunk; clean RX tails remain available, and TE or ambiguous completion permanently quarantines resources.
RX gaps may lose frames with no overrun indication; FE/PE reports promptly but recovery waits for the old DMA count.
TX requires TX, RX requires RX, combined construction requires both signals and independent static staging/channels.
No DMA RTS/CTS, continuous RX, borrowed zero-copy, early abort, throughput or finite-liveness guarantee.
Evidence identities are the current external authority; historical project/output hashes are not a runtime gate.
All selections retain their current own-family route, package, alias, memory and HAL exclusion policy.
Nine selected example tuples bind routes and memory; a source checker does not establish that any tuple was built or executed.
Runtime correctness, shared-vector lifecycle and cancellation/forget interleavings require separate final-source review.
Software BufferOverflow is distinct from native Overrun; software precedence ORE > PE > FE > NE is not vendor arbitration.
No exact lost-character count, throughput, latency, lossless reception or RTS queue-watermark guarantee.
